subject: Post-call: PrivateSite hosting qualification — dataflow, network constraints, next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@privatesite.io>, Priya Sharma <priya@privatesite.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — PrivateSite hosting qualification (dataflow, network constraints, next steps)

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all have a single source of truth.

Key pain points you shared:
- Data residency requirement: all customer PII and model logs must remain inside your AWS account / us-east-1 and not be persistent in a public Redwood tenancy.
- Network isolation: preferred air-gapped-style posture with no outbound internet egress from inference hosts; only a management control plane over a customer-managed bastion is acceptable.
- Procurement & timeline: procurement window ~6–9 weeks, but technical POC helps speed internal approvals.
- Cost sensitivity for sustained throughput: prefer guidance on quantization/instance sizing to balance latency vs cost.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC-hosted control plane) or on-prem package with no public egress and KMS integration.
- Two hosting patterns we recommend for your topology: VPC Peering with routed private subnets OR an isolated on-prem inference cluster with periodic secure sync.
- POC path: 2-week controlled POC in your staging account (limited traffic) to validate connectivity, KV cache behavior, and egress rules.

Requested items from your side (asks):
1) Network diagram (at least a /16-ish diagram showing subnets, NAT/IGW, transit gateways, firewall appliances).
2) List of CIDR ranges and any port/host restrictions (eg, outbound only to management bastion at 10.10.50.12:443).
3) Compliance contact for DPA/technical security artifacts (SOC2, retention, logging).
4) Target week(s) for a POC (we suggested May 31–Jun 11 as possible windows).

Next steps (tentative):
- Jonás/Ben: draft POC SOW and minimal IAM/network config by end of week. (Attachment: redwood-product-sheet.pdf — feature + hosting summary)
- PrivateSite: share network diagram and compliance lead.
- Redwood SE (Ben): propose two concrete architecture options with ports and exemplar SG rules.

If I missed anything or got something wrong, please correct inline. Happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-product-sheet.pdf

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@privatesite.io>

Date: 2027-05-18T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — PrivateSite hosting qualification (dataflow, network constraints, next steps)

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

On network/isolation:
- We cannot allow direct outbound internet egress from inference hosts. All outbound management traffic must be proxied through our management bastion (10.10.50.12) and only to a pinned set of IPs you provide.
- We currently use a transit gateway and Palo Alto firewalls; any recommended SG rules will need to be expressible as source/dest IP + port.

On data residency and logs:
- Model inputs and outputs must not persist in a Redwood-managed multi-tenant storage. Short-lived KV/cache allowed if it is contained within our VPC and encrypted with our KMS.

On POC timing:
- Procurement is kicking off next week; earliest we can commit engineering time is Jun 7. A short 1–2 week POC is preferred (staging traffic only).

I've attached a one-page network summary we use for partners — it lists NAT behavior and current firewall egress rules.

Alex
Head of Infrastructure | PrivateSite
alex.rivera@privatesite.io

Attachments: privatesite-network-summary.pdf

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — PrivateSite hosting qualification (dataflow, network constraints, next steps)

Alex / Priya — appreciate the detail. A few concrete technical notes and a proposed POC config to help your infra team evaluate: 

1) Two recommended hosting patterns (tradeoffs):
  a) VPC Peering + Private Control Plane (fast to stand up, low latency). In this pattern RW hosts run in your account and communicate to our control plane over a small set of pinned IPs — all over port 443 — with strict SGs. No model artifacts are stored in our multi-tenant store.
  b) On-prem/air-gapped inference cluster (for maximum isolation). We run an appliance/container bundle you deploy behind your firewall; telemetry is pushed only when permitted via your bastion. Higher ops lift but meets strict regulatory needs.

2) Ports/IPs and non-negotiables:
  - Management (control plane) egress: to 54.23.12.87:443 (Redwood management) OR to an endpoint we host in your account (we can do private link).
  - Peering route requirements: allow routes between our subnets and your inference subnets for intra-VPC traffic.
  - KMS: We support using your KMS for at-rest model key wrapping — helpful for compliance.

3) POC proposal (staging):
  - Duration: 7–10 days (staging only).
  - Deliverables: connectivity validation, end-to-end inferencing with synthetic load, latency profile, KV cache behavior, and cost estimate.
  - Minimal config: two inference nodes (g4dn-like), one small control-plane proxy, test harness.

4) Next technical artifacts we will provide by Friday: detailed SG/CIDR list, example IAM role templates, and a short SOW for the POC (redwood-poc-sow.docx). I'm attaching our internal hosting checklist to make approvals easier.

If that aligns, we can lock Jun 7–18 as POC weeks and I will loop in our infra engineer to coordinate a short runbook.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: hosting-checklist.csv, redwood-poc-sow.docx
